name: Modernist Graphic Design
visualIdentity: Supplemental reference, not a claim about a source collection’s named style. Function first: simplified forms, shared alignment, clear reading order, limited colors, and hierarchy through size and placement. Animate structural or informational change without decorative motion.
suitableUses: Explicit good fits include UI and product storytelling, editorial and minimalist layouts, motion posters, and staged geometric compositions. Hybrids can explain processes, organizations, onboarding, infrastructure, logistics, or product architecture. These are suitability judgments, not requirements.
limitations: Adapt or omit motion that changes hierarchy without clarifying the subject, crops important details, pushes text into unsafe areas, or disrupts page layout. Card stacks can hide essential copy or provenance; carousels can impair simultaneous comparison or long reading; chapters need meaningful boundaries. Avoid nested patterns with conflicting progress drivers or unreadable motion.
palette: For new artwork only when no approved palette exists, a suggested three-color set is background #FAF8F2, foreground #202020, and subordinate blue accent #235DA8. These are suggestions, not canonical colors. Preserve task, brand, reference, semantic-role, asset, and visual-cue color constraints; normalize equivalent notation only. Use discrete colors; gradients are disabled. Suggested opaque text pairs meet the 4.5 target, but inspect actual compositing and readability. Improve contrast through placement or existing backing, not recoloring.
motionAndInteraction: Use continuous, hierarchy-preserving movement to explain change, with readable holds and deliberate cuts or impacts where appropriate. For video, derive every state from seekable composition time, including direct and reverse seeks; never depend on live input. For interactive HTML, scroll progress may drive pinned hero recomposition, bounded card stacking, chapter handoffs, or story steps; release pins without jumps. A horizontal carousel can use swipe, buttons, or keyboard and must settle at a defined selection. Check touch, keyboard, and reduced-motion behavior.
audio: Unspecified; no fixed soundtrack, genre, tempo, voice, or sound layer is required. Choose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic, audience, story, and explicit audio requirements. Use authorized assets, leave speech clear, avoid clipping, and synchronize and inspect audio with picture.
assetRequirements: Use real text and shared layout measurements; suitable style renderers include browser HTML/CSS and SVG for typography, layout, shapes, icons, and masks. Supply or create task-appropriate images, diagrams, fonts, and audio; exact assets and copy are unspecified. Preserve source colors. Optional tldraw can author diagrams/cards for export; flattened assets need deliberate layers if elements animate separately.
combinations: Style alone suits functional layouts. With style-109 connector diagrams, order modules, connectors, then labels; use dark connectors and blue only for the active path. With style-108 shallow isometric diagrams, keep labels flat, use neutral tints from existing tokens, and mark the active component blue. Avoid tangled lines, support-palette warm accents, 3D lighting, rotated labels, and perspective shrinkage. These combinations suit explanatory systems; use only when they clarify relationships.
productionApproach: Select visual and motion tools by style, action, assets, and fidelity; assign one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the primary composition/export pipeline; Remotion is allowed only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, with the reason recorded. Neither dictates visual construction. Use deterministic time-driven layers; GSAP is the recommended seekable timeline, while Motion is optional and requires verified synchronization. Validate key frames, full playback, dimensions, timing, audio sync, and loop continuity.
